featured_reviews.name: Prachi Nanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
I came to Dr. Manjiri just three weeks before my due date — a last-minute switch from my original doctor who had to travel during my birth.

I went past my due date and she agreed to wait patiently for spontaneous labour. On the day, she arrived at the hospital before we even did, and during active labour she was a quiet, steady presence in the room — making a suggestion or providing guidance only when it truly mattered.

And when I pushed my baby, her calm and capable hands were right there doing what needed to be done. My son arrived safely, and after the birth, she became a completely different energy — peaceful and calm, entirely focused on that first bond between mother and child. It felt less like a delivery room and more like a sacred space.

In a world where obstetric care has become increasingly intervention-driven — where the default is to hurry, to medicate, to manage — Dr. Manjirir has taken the road less travelled. She understands that birth, when supported rather than controlled, has its own intelligence. It is not a popular choice in today's medical landscape, and I imagine it takes real conviction to hold that line. But she does. Quietly, consistently, without fanfare.

I had an unmedicated water birth, overdue, with a cord around my baby, and yet I walked away feeling like my body had been trusted and my birth had been honoured. That is an extraordinary thing to be able to say.

If you are looking for a doctor who will hold space for the birth you hope for — rather than the one that's most convenient — Dr. Manjiri is who you want in that room.

I am writing this with immense gratitude and respect in my heart for Dr Aparna ma'am who came like a blessing in my life when I was at my lowest. I was completely hopeless and even had negative self harming thoughts at times because of the medical trauma due to my prolonged illness. I have been dealing with recurrent UTIs since my early puberty and had incontinence issues since childhood too. I used to get sudden urge to go to the toilet which lead to me developing a bad habit of holding pee. Later during my puberty I got back to back UTIs and burning sensations. I also had constipation since this time. In 2014 (15 yrs old) I first time went to doctor with complain of burning sensation and got diagnosed with UTI. The doctor prescribed me medicines including antibiotics and gels. As I grew up the issue didn't seem to resolve despite visiting multiple doctors and getting many treatments. By 2018 I started having extreme pain around my whole pelvic area that includes my bladder and urethra and was given multiple oral antibiotics and even prescribed Intravenous antibiotics for 2 weeks after oral medicine stopped affecting fot my infections. By this time I had already visited multiple doctors but in 2019-2020, Covid 19 outbreak happened and I could not continue my treatments and I suffered immense pain. Later in 2021 I went to SGPGI, Lucknow where multiple check ups and treatments were given. I was referred to the Anesthesia dept for pain management since the urology meds were not helping with the pain. I had to go through excruciating pain which lasted for 15 hours a day and this happened on a daily basis.I was also given 2 nerve blocks (in 2021 - 2022) to stop the pain, both of which did not work unfortunately. I also developed a gynecological issue and noticed a lump near my urethra which was a cyst like protrusion from the mucosa lining. I got checked by a Gynecologist who could not diagnose its root cause. However, in 2024, I got admitted twice again in Sgpgi where my cystoscopy was done and only inflammation was reported in my bladder referring to severe cystitis.

When I met her for the first time she talked to me with motherly care and assured me that I will be cured. She was were very patient and attentive and made sure that I get comfortable to tell her about the symptoms thoroughly and gave a lot of time and attention to each and every single detail. I could open up before her freely because of her caring and kind nature. After going through all my reports from previous 14 years of treatments she did several test and one of which was the sonography at Cama where she is an Assistant Professor and works pro bono. After all the tests my proper diagnosis was done and it was severe cystitis as well as the lump. She suggested several treatments including surgery, cystoscopy, hydrodistension as well as bladder instillations. She has also helped me financially and upon my request she did my surgery for cyst and a cystoscopy with hydrodistension at Cama Hospital. I was under a lot stress about the finances and the co-operation and understanding from my doctor but she made it seemless for me and I am actually in amaze how everything has turned out after so many years of hopelessness. I am recovering better now with the help of medications and instillations as adviced by her.

I truly dont believe any amount of words would be enough to express my gratitude to Dr Aparna Ma'am and her staff who were very very co-operating and kind and made me comfortable throughout the tests and appointments. I received her help in a way I could not have imagined. She is an amazing doctor and is very passionate about her work and a great philanthropist too. I admire her deep sense of service and the way she addresses and assures her patients. The way she counsel her patients is itself so helpful that brings out faith and hope to fight and overcome the illness and I wish her and Doctors like her always be blessed. A true gift to mankind. :)

featured_reviews.name: sunetra Rathnam
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dr Piyush Goyal is truly an exceptional gynaecologist, and I would wholeheartedly recommend him to anyone dealing with complex gynaecological health conditions especially endometriosis and adenomyosis.

My journey began when I was just 19 years old  confused, frightened, and in unbearable pain. My father happened to read an article about Dr. Piyush Goyal in The Times of India that spoke about his expertise in handling complex gynecological cases. That moment changed everything. Through him, we finally understood what I had been struggling with severe endometriosis and adenomyosis. I met him in 2010, and I have been his patient ever since for 16 years now.

These conditions brought not just chronic pelvic pain, but extreme, life-disrupting pain that affected every part of my daily functioning. Over time, my disease also involved other organs like my intestines and bowel, leading to serious complications that made even basic bodily functions difficult and exhausting. Anyone who lives with advanced endometriosis and adenomyosis understands how physically and emotionally draining this can be.

Endometriosis is a recurring and highly unpredictable disease, and no two patients experience it the same way. Over the years, Dr. Piyush has operated on me three times, and each time I have come out with a better quality of life, reduced pain, and renewed hope. That itself speaks volumes about his expertise.

What truly sets him apart is not just his surgical skill, but his depth of understanding and clarity in communication. He explains every aspect of the disease in a way that makes you feel informed, prepared, and reassured. He combines modern medical advancements, cutting-edge technology, and years of clinical experience  yet always follows a conservative, patient-first approach. He never rushes into aggressive intervention and always prioritizes long-term wellbeing while carefully avoiding complications.

With a chronic condition this complex, trust is everything  and I trust him completely. Through years of surgeries, recovery, uncertainty, and pain, he has been the one constant source of confidence and reassurance in my treatment journey.

I can say with complete honesty that no one could have explained, diagnosed, and treated my condition better. Living with severe endometriosis and adenomyosis is not easy, but having a doctor who genuinely understands the disease  and the person living with it makes all the difference.

I am deeply grateful for the care, compassion, and life-changing difference he has made over the past 16 years. He is not just an outstanding doctor, he truly transforms lives.

featured_reviews.name: Prayasha Chaudhary
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dr. Piyush Goyal is an exceptional gynecologist & I would recommend him to anyone suffering from reproductive health issues, especially endometriosis.

I was diagnosed with endometriosis two years ago while visiting Nepal. I had to undergo an emergency cystectomy with post-surgical complications. The anesthesia lasted over 24 hours & once awake, I was throwing up 20-25 times a day. I was allergic to the meds being injected but the doctors refused to address it. I ended up staying in the hospital for a week. Moreover, the surgeon had only removed the cyst but not treated the disease. Post surgery, I was put on 2mg of Dinogest for 1.5 years. Then, a lump occurred in my breast (biopsy determined it fibroadenoma). Doctors in Nepal asked me to be off Dinogest for a few months. Shortly after discontinuing the medication, I experienced severe abdominal pain & was on bed rest for a month. I visited multiple doctors in Nepal to seek pain relief, but faced only disappointments. I decided to consult a doctor in Delhi who recommended Mirena. She was a gynecologist but had not dealt a lot with endometriosis cases. Mirena insertion experience was extremely painful, & I was partly immobile for 2 months.

After 2 months of excruciating pain across my abdomen & leg, I was referred to Dr. Goyal by a friend who had undergone a laparoscopic surgery for endometriosis herself. I met Dr. Goyal in January, & it was the first time a doctor properly explained what endometriosis is & what it does to my body. It was my first time in Mumbai, so Dr. Goyal & his team helped me get all the required appointments for my lab work. MRI showed very tiny cysts in my right ovary & given my pain, I was ready to undergo surgery. Dr. Goyal was very patient & recommended not undergoing a procedure right away & waiting to see if Mirena’s side effects would settle. I was impressed to hear Dr. Goyal take a non-surgical stance because all the doctors in Nepal were pressuring me to undergo surgery & remove my ovaries. Dr. Goyal suggested a follow up in 2 months. During the 2-month waiting period we did bi-weekly check-ins through WhatsApp. He had asked me to keep my daily pain scores which evidently showed continuation of my pain & was gradually getting worse. Dr. Goyal recommended a TVS/USG. USG showed a 7x5x3cm cyst in my left ovary. There weren’t any indications if it was a simple cyst or an endometriotic cyst but gave Dr. Goyal a reason to finally look inside.

On April 1st, I underwent a hysteroscopy, both ovarian cystectomy, endometriotic fulguration, & hysteroscopic Mirena removal at Surya Hospital lead by Dr. Goyal. Before the surgery, we were precisely explained, consulted by Dr. Goyal for over an hours on procedures and plan of action. Having that conversation put me at ease & made going into the surgery very comfortable. During the surgery, Dr. Goyal was able to restore my ovaries, fallopian tubes, & uterus to the right places which were either stuck together or on the walls of my abdomen. He was also able to remove the nodules that were causing my leg pain, as well as infection sacks caused by improper care from my last surgery in Nepal. Two hours after the surgery, I was up & feeling very comfortable. Dr. Goyal & his team were very attentive to my aftercare. Dr. Goyal consistently checked on my health by coming in person as well as through WhatsApp. The entire procedure was a breeze compared to my past experiences thanks to Dr. Goyal. I got discharged on the second day post-op feeling fresh & was fully mobile without painkillers by day 3.

I feel significantly better, & my pain has completely subsided. I am very thankful I got referred to Dr. Goyal & was able to go through my procedure with him. He was extremely thorough with his investigation & explanations. He made me feel very comfortable before & after my procedure, & I feel confident that this time my recovery will be successful.

Dr. Goyal's experience and knowledge superseded my expectations. He really is a one-of-a-kind doctor, & I would 100% recommend him!

"I have an ovarian cyst. Do I need surgery?"

This is one of the most common questions I hear in my OPD — and the honest answer is: it depends. Not every ovarian cyst needs to be operated upon. But some absolutely should not be ignored.

Here is a simple way to think about it:

Watchful waiting is often appropriate when:
👁️ The cyst is small — typically under 5 cm
👁️ It appears simple and fluid-filled on ultrasound
👁️ You have no significant symptoms
👁️ It is likely a functional cyst that may resolve on its own

Surgery is worth discussing when:
🔬 The cyst is larger than 5–6 cm or is growing on follow-up scans
🔬 The ultrasound shows complex features — solid areas or internal divisions
🔬 You are experiencing pain, persistent bloating, or a feeling of fullness
🔬 The cyst is suspected to be an endometrioma or a dermoid

When surgery is needed, laparoscopic cystectomy allows precise removal of the cyst while preserving the healthy ovarian tissue — through just a few tiny keyhole incisions.

If you have recently been told you have an ovarian cyst and are unsure what to do next, a proper evaluation will give you clarity.

Endometriosis happens when tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus, causing inflammation, pain, and sometimes fertility difficulties. The earlier it's identified, the more treatment options remain available.

Some signs worth taking seriously:

🔸 Period pain severe enough to disrupt daily life or work
🔸 Pain during or after intimacy
🔸 Pain with bowel movements or urination, especially during periods

🔸 Difficulty conceiving without an obvious cause
